title: TP hang repro harness: mixed prefill/decode workload config (tunable concurrency + seq distributions)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context: We need a deterministic-ish repro for the most common TP hang signature we’re seeing under sustained load: mixed prefill + streaming decode with bursty concurrency and a long-tail prompt length distribution. This PR adds a benchmark-lab harness configuration and driver utilities to reproduce the hang (or at minimum force the same scheduler/comms pressure pattern) with knobs we can sweep in perf-lab/perf-canary.

What this adds: (1) New scenario config `scenarios/tp/mixed_prefill_decode_hang.yaml` with tunable parameters: tp_degree, max_inflight_requests, client_concurrency, prompt_length_distribution (mixture model), decode_tokens_distribution, streaming_enabled, cancellation_rate, and request_interarrival_ms distribution; (2) A small workload generator `bench/workloads/mixed_prefill_decode.py` that produces request traces with stable seeds and emits a compact trace summary so runs are comparable; (3) A runner wrapper `bin/run_tp_hang_repro` that standardizes invocation (env, logging, timeouts), tags the run with a `repro_signature=tp_mixed_prefill_decode_v1`, and writes artifacts (trace + summary + selected runtime logs) to the usual benchmark-lab artifact dir; (4) A “stall detection mode” that treats no-progress (no tokens streamed + no heartbeat log lines from runtime) for N seconds as a failure, so the harness terminates and captures state rather than hanging forever.

Notes / constraints: This harness does not attempt to “fix” the runtime; it’s intended to produce a repeatable pressure pattern and make it easy to compare before/after changes (scheduler guardrails, NCCL sync hardening, watchdog). The default knobs are conservative to avoid false positives on smaller GPUs; for A100/H100, the default preset `--preset a100_80g_tp4` matches the incident workload shape we’ve been triaging.

How to run (example): `./bin/run_tp_hang_repro --target dedicated:bench-lab-a100 --scenario scenarios/tp/mixed_prefill_decode_hang.yaml --set tp_degree=4 --set client_concurrency=96 --set max_inflight_requests=256 --set prompt_length_distribution=mixture:short=0.7,mid=0.2,long=0.1 --seed 1337 --timeout_s 900`.

Outputs: (a) `artifacts/<run_id>/trace.jsonl` with per-request prompt_len/decode_len/streaming flags and timestamps; (b) `artifacts/<run_id>/summary.json` (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cancellations, failures, stall windows); (c) `artifacts/<run_id>/runtime_excerpt.log` (tail + relevant grep lines for NCCL/scheduler) to speed up triage.

Testing: Unit tests cover trace generation determinism (seeded), config parsing, and stall detector behavior. GPU execution is validated in perf-lab; CI runs the generator + parser tests and a dry-run that exercises the scenario end-to-end without hitting a real runtime.

Follow-ups: This should be paired with ENG-4823 (heartbeat metrics) once those log/metric names settle so the stall detector can key off structured signals rather than log heuristics.
commits: Add mixed prefill/decode scenario YAML with sweepable knobs
Implement deterministic request trace generator (mixture prompt lengths + bursty arrivals)
Add runner wrapper with standardized logging, artifacts, and timeout handling
Add stall detector + failure artifact capture path
Unit tests for config parsing + trace determinism
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can we ensure the distribution spec is stable and human-readable? I’m worried people will tweak YAML and accidentally change semantics. Suggest a strict parser + echo normalized distribution in the summary.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added normalization + canonical string form in `summary.json` (`prompt_length_distribution_canonical`). Also fail fast if weights don’t sum to ~1.0.

Marcus Reed (review): For regression coverage, we need this to exit on stall and produce artifacts. Can we guarantee a hard timeout even if the client blocks? Also: please include a single-line ‘run signature’ we can grep in logs.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `--timeout_s` enforced via watchdog thread; on timeout we stop sending new requests, dump trace/summary, and exit non-zero. Also added `repro_signature=tp_mixed_prefill_decode_v1` tag in summary and runner stdout.

Noah Patel (review): The cancellation rate knob is important, but make sure it’s not on by default; otherwise we’ll conflate cancellation bugs with collective starvation. Also can we support disabling streaming while keeping mixed prefill/decode characteristics?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Default `cancellation_rate=0.0` and `streaming_enabled=true` (matches current incident shape). Added `streaming_enabled=false` path that still uses mixed prefill/decode by issuing chunked decode polling requests.

Kira Volkov (review): CI should not require GPUs, but should validate that scenario config loads and generates trace with non-empty distributions. Add a small dry-run test and document minimum Python deps.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `tests/test_scenario_dry_run.py` (no network) and updated docs for deps + expected outputs. CI now runs dry-run job.
Marcus Reed (approval): LGTM. This is good enough to start gating fixes. Please file follow-up to key off heartbeat metrics once ENG-4823 merges.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Filed follow-up note in ENG-4822 + linked in doc.
release_notes: Adds benchmark-lab TP hang repro scenario (mixed prefill/decode) with deterministic trace generation, stall detection, and standardized artifacts for perf-lab runs.
